message.reasoning_content:
The watch is a Patek Philippe Nautilus with a black dial, annual calendar with power reserve indicator, moonphase... Actually this looks like the Nautilus 5712/1A-001 — but wait, the 5712 has a moonphase at the bottom left subdial and a date with pointer... Let me think.

The 5712/1A-001 has: small seconds subdial at 4-5 o'clock, power reserve indicator at 10-11, date subdial with pointer at 7-8 o'clock with moonphase inside it. Yes — the image shows a date subdial at the lower left with numbers 1-29-31, and inside it a moon phase aperture. And a small seconds at lower right. Power reserve at top left with "2 4 6" markings. Dial is black-gray gradient with horizontal embossed pattern.

So reference is 5712/1A-001. Stainless steel, metal bracelet, automatic (caliber 240 PS IRM C LU).

Confidence high ~0.9.

Model family: Nautilus.

Movement: automatic. Case material: stainless-steel. Bracelet: metal.

Note the dial appears black/grey — the 5712/1A-001 has a black-blue gradient. There's also a titanium 5712/1A? No. There's the 5712G white gold with leather strap. This one clearly has steel bracelet with black dial. Some newer versions: 5712/1A-001 (2006-2022ish). Reference 5712/1A-001 is the classic.

Confidence 0.85.

Model family: "Nautilus" — maybe "Nautilus 5712". I'll say "Nautilus".
